source_text: Quantum igitur inter te et Paulum distet, intende. Ille dicit: Per unum hominem [n94] , tu: Per duos, id est, per generationem. Ille pronuntiat, in primo homine et peccatum et mortem fuisse, ad posteros vero solam transisse mortem; tu contra asseris, et peccatum ad omnes et interitum cucurrisse.
pass_a_gloss: How much therefore lies between you and Paul, attend. He says: Through one human being, you: Through two, that is, through generation. He pronounces that in the first human being both sin and death were, but that to posterity only death passed; you against assert that both sin and destruction ran to all.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: Consider, then, the distance between you and Paul. He says ‘through one man’ (Romans 5:12); you say ‘through two,’ that is, through generation. He declares that both sin and death were in the first man, but that only death passed to his descendants. You, on the contrary, maintain that both sin and destruction spread to everyone.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
